name: A J Packaging
summary: A J Packaging, incorporated in Hyderabad in 1995, makes oval, rectangular and round metal tin cans for FMCG and paint makers such as Asian Paints, Haldiram's and CCL Products, from plants in Hyderabad and Ghaziabad. Revenue fell from ₹210 cr in FY24 to ₹193 cr in FY25 and then rose to ₹223 cr in FY26, while profit after tax rose 54.5% to ₹7.9 cr in FY26, though the net margin is still thin at 3.6%. The ₹54 cr issue is mostly fresh money (₹49.5 cr), and the DRHP put ₹24.5 cr towards working capital and ₹7 cr towards repaying loans; debt to equity was 1.69 before the issue. At the upper band the post-issue P/E is about 23.9x, just below the 26.1x median of listed peers, but the price to book of about 2.0x is well above theirs, and the top ten customers bring in about 70% of revenue.

fh1.finding: Revenue went from ₹210.03 cr (FY24) to ₹223.03 cr (FY26), a CAGR of only about 3.0%.

fh2.finding: Revenue fell to ₹193.46 cr in FY25 from ₹210.03 cr in FY24, then rose to ₹223.03 cr in FY26.

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 1.69 in FY26 (borrowings ₹75.00 cr vs net worth ₹44.46 cr).

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose about 6.9% (₹70.13 cr in FY24 to ₹75.00 cr in FY26), slightly faster than revenue (+6.2%).

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹26.69 cr, ₹37.32 cr, ₹44.46 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was ₹15.75 cr in FY26, about twice the ₹7.91 cr profit.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew 54.5% in FY26, from ₹5.12 cr to ₹7.91 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from 1.80% (FY24) to 2.64% (FY25) and 3.55% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 17.79% in FY26, up from 13.71% in FY25.

pr4.finding: ROCE was 17.41% in FY26, up from 15.32% in FY25.

pr5.finding: Peer profit or EBITDA margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 23.9x (₹189.09 cr market cap on 1,05,05,245 shares at ₹180 ÷ ₹7.91 cr FY26 PAT) vs a peer median of 26.1x (Shetron 26.1x, Kaira Can 69.8x, Rajeshwari Cans 6.6x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 2.0x (₹189.09 cr ÷ ₹93.96 cr, i.e. ₹44.46 cr FY26 net worth + ₹49.5 cr fresh issue) vs a peer median of 1.38x, about 46% above.

va3.finding: Post-issue market cap to FY26 revenue is about 0.85x (₹189.09 cr ÷ ₹223.03 cr), but peer market cap to sales figures were not found.

va4.finding: No details of share issues or transfers in the 12 months before the IPO were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 66.07% after the issue, down from 92.72%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: No information on regulatory action against promoters or directors was found.

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹4.50 cr (2.5 lakh shares by promoter Ranjani Agarwal), about 8.3% of the ₹54 cr issue.

is2.finding: The ₹54 cr issue is about 28.6% of the ₹189.09 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: The average acquisition cost of the selling promoter's shares was not found in public sources.

up1.finding: The DRHP puts ₹24.5 cr into working capital and ₹7 cr into loan repayment; none of the fresh issue funds new capex, expansion or acquisitions.

up2.finding: ₹7.00 cr, about 14% of the ₹49.5 cr fresh issue, goes to repaying loans (DRHP figure).

up3.finding: The amount for general corporate purposes was not stated in public sources.

up4.finding: Public sources don't say whose loans are being repaid.

lg1.finding: Litigation amounts were not found in public sources.

lg2.finding: No information on criminal or regulatory cases was found.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: The top ten customers bring in about 70% of revenue, with no long-term agreements.

rk2.finding: Dependence on a few suppliers for most raw materials is called out as a risk; exact shares are not published.

rk3.finding: Incorporated on 6 July 1995, so over 31 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
